lede: Tuesday was a risk-off day across global markets. The Nasdaq 100 fell nearly 2%, gold dropped more than 2% and Bitcoin slid below $60,000, pushing the Fear & Greed Index to 11 — deep in Extreme Fear territory. Jakarta and the Dow Jones were the exceptions, both closing modestly higher.

paras: The IHSG went against the global tide, rising 0.49% to close at 5,241.59 while most major markets fell. Indonesian stocks held their ground on a day when risk appetite faded almost everywhere else.
Bank Indonesia was active on the day, publishing its November monetary policy review and the results of its floating-rate note (BI-FRN) auction held on 24 November.

US stocks split. The Nasdaq 100 led the decline, down 1.99% to 638.10, and the S&P 500 slipped 0.49% to 718.78. The Dow Jones went the other way, gaining 0.79% to 499.74, as money rotated away from growth and into steadier names.
Geopolitics made the wire too: the US Treasury announced an operation disrupting Iran's global shadow banking networks, identifying nearly $15 billion in potential Iranian shadow banking activity.
Crypto followed the risk-off mood. Bitcoin fell 2.35% to $59,832, slipping under the $60,000 mark, while Ethereum dropped 1.79% to $1,680.11.
Sentiment matched the price action. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index read 11 — Extreme Fear — its lowest kind of reading, reflecting how quickly nerves have spread across the market.

title: Tech and Crypto Tumble as Fear Grips the Markets
